summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; one web search used). All three questions are PENDING: no tariff, export price, value-added or reliability value was retrieved. Q1 (realised export price vs ERC industrial tariff) is designed as a comparison at the generator busbar in NPR_per_MWh, with INR converted at the NRB NPR/INR middle rate for the same month, demand charges converted only via a stated load-factor range, and the export price taken from 22E/22B (not re-derived). Q2 (value added per GWh) is designed as a bounded marginal estimate: census average VA per GWh from the NSO National Industrial Survey 2019/20 (11th round of the Census of Manufacturing Establishments series, located by search) and CME 2011/12 as the upper bound; price paid for electricity as the lower bound; project-level marginal VA net of annualised capital and labour at a shadow wage for cement, steel, data centres, green hydrogen/ammonia, with electric cooking and transport valued as import substitution. Q3 (reliability) is designed as reliability classes (continuous, shift, flexible), a baseline of SAIDI/SAIFI, grid disturbances and Enterprise Survey outage indicators, and a costing of dedicated supply and unserved energy delivered to 22E as C_GRID. Aligned with 22E: 05B supplies T_IND, VA_IND, K_IND and the reliability part of C_GRID and does not duplicate the opportunity-cost table.

findings.claim: Q1. ERC industrial consumer tariff schedule in force: energy charge by supply voltage (LV, MV 11 kV, MV 33 kV, HV 66/132 kV) and time-of-day block, with any seasonal differentiation.
findings.period: tariff order in force FY2082/83 (2025/26) and FY2083/84 (2026/27); earlier orders back to FY2078/79 for the time series
findings.note: Data required: the tariff-order table for each industrial category (and dedicated/trunk-line categories). Record order date, effective date and vintage. Category labels in the order take precedence over the voltage labels used here.

findings.claim: Q1. ERC industrial demand charge by supply voltage and dedicated-feeder status.
findings.note: Native unit is NPR per kVA per month, which has no code in units.py (challenge to 00A); recorded without unit until added. Converted to NPR_per_kWh only through a stated load-factor and power-factor range (22E-A4, 05B-A3).

findings.claim: Q1. Realised average industrial tariff = NEA industrial revenue / industrial energy sold, per Nepal FY (includes demand charges, ToD mix, surcharges and rebates).
findings.note: Data required: NEA annual report table of sales (kWh) and revenue (NPR) by consumer category. Cross-check against implied price paid in NIS 2019/20 (electricity expenditure / kWh purchased) for FY2019/20.

findings.claim: Q1. Realised export price per MWh (NEA export revenue / export energy) by route and Nepali month, as the comparator to the industrial tariff.
findings.note: Not re-derived here: taken from 22E parameter P_EXP / 22B decomposition once observed. 05B only aligns units and the metering point (see tariff_comparison).

findings.claim: Q1. NPR per INR reference rate (middle of buying and selling) by month, used to express INR-denominated export prices in NPR at the same period.
findings.note: Peg rate must be retrieved from NRB, not assumed; peg regime statement from the Monetary Policy document.

findings.claim: Q1. Implied electricity price actually paid by manufacturing establishments, by ISIC industry (electricity expenditure / kWh purchased).
findings.note: Checks whether tariff-order categories map to what industry actually pays (penalties, minimum charges, captive generation excluded).

findings.claim: Q2. Average manufacturing value added per GWh of purchased electricity by ISIC industry (4-digit where cells allow, else 2-digit), current prices.
findings.note: VA_IND upper-bound input to 22E. Average ratio only; NOT marginal. Suppressed cells and establishments with own generation reported separately.

findings.claim: Q2. Electricity cost share of gross output and of value added by ISIC industry.
findings.note: Used for the cost-share (lower-bound) marginal-product method and to classify electricity-intensive industries for 05C RCA flags.

findings.claim: Q2. Electricity intensity (GWh per NPR mn of VA) by ISIC industry - hand-off requested by 22E and 05C.
findings.note: Reported as GWh / NPR_current_mn; 'ratio' used because units.py has no compound intensity code (challenge to 00A).

findings.claim: Q2. Marginal value added per GWh for new cement grinding / integrated cement capacity in Nepal, net of annualised capital charge and labour at shadow wage.
findings.note: Requires ISIC 2394 NIS cell, DoInd/IBN project capital cost per tonne capacity, IEA kWh/t as transfer assumption, clinker/cement import prices from customs.

findings.claim: Q2. Marginal value added per GWh for new steel melting (induction/electric-arc billets) and re-rolling capacity, net of capital and labour at shadow wage.
findings.note: ISIC 2410/2431 NIS cells; scrap/sponge-iron/billet import prices (customs HS 7203/7204/7207).

findings.claim: Q2. Marginal value added per GWh for data centres (ISIC 6311), net of capital (incl. backup) and labour at shadow wage.
findings.note: Not covered by the manufacturing census; requires project documents or labelled international reference; export-of-services revenue and foreign-owned profit repatriation (GNI vs GDP) handled separately.

findings.claim: Q2. Marginal value added per GWh for electrolytic hydrogen and ammonia/urea (import substitution of fertiliser), including capacity-factor effect when operated on wet-season surplus only.
findings.note: No Nepal production; entirely transfer assumptions from IEA/IRENA plus customs urea import prices. Capital charge per GWh rises sharply at low capacity factor.

findings.claim: Q2. Net national value per GWh of electric cooking (household LPG substitution): avoided LPG import cost (and subsidy) per GWh minus appliance and distribution-reinforcement cost.
findings.note: Not industrial value added: value is import substitution and welfare (indoor air quality) - enters MarginalUseComparison in place of domestic_value_added_per_gwh only with explicit labelling.

findings.claim: Q2. Net national value per GWh of electric transport (EV cars, two-wheelers, buses; charging): avoided petrol/diesel imports per GWh minus vehicle premium and charging-infrastructure cost.
findings.note: Import-substitution netback; EV import tariff policy changes affect the vehicle premium.

findings.claim: Q2. Capital cost per unit capacity and annual electricity use per unit capacity (hence annualised capital charge per GWh, K_IND) for each candidate industry.
findings.note: Delivered to 22E as K_IND. Discount rate and asset life are assumptions to be taken from the shared register (config/model_config.yaml), not set here.

findings.claim: Q3. Distribution reliability indices (SAIDI, SAIFI) by NEA distribution centre / province, and for industrial and dedicated feeders where reported.
findings.note: SAIDI native unit is hours or minutes per customer per year; units.py lacks hours/minutes (challenge to 00A), recorded without unit until added. Availability of these indices in NEA publications is unconfirmed.

findings.claim: Q3. Frequency of interruptions per customer per year (SAIFI) on industrial feeders.
findings.note: Count per customer per year; definition (momentary interruptions included or not) to record.

findings.claim: Q3. System-wide grid disturbances / blackouts and forced outages of the INPS by month.
findings.note: From NEA system operation / load dispatch reports.

findings.claim: Q3. Firm-reported outages in a typical month, losses due to outages as share of sales, and share of firms with generators (Nepal, latest Enterprise Survey round).
findings.period: latest Enterprise Survey round for Nepal (calendar-year fieldwork; year to record)
findings.note: Firm-perceived reliability baseline; calendar-year survey not mixed with Nepal FY series without note.

findings.claim: Q3. Unit investment cost of dedicated industrial supply: 132/33 kV substation capacity, dedicated 33 kV/11 kV feeders, trunk lines, reactive compensation; and the tariff/contribution rules by which industry pays for them.
findings.note: Converted to per-GWh (C_GRID reliability component) with the candidate industry's load factor; delivered to 22E.

findings.claim: Q3. Dry-season firm-supply requirement for continuous-process industry: capacity (MW) that must be met by imports or storage hydro in import-marginal months.
findings.note: Links to 05A seasonal profile and 22E P_IMP; the reliability of a continuous load in the dry season depends on Indian import approvals (see challenge to 28).

findings.claim: Tariff and export price are compared at a common metering point and currency: all values expressed in NPR_per_MWh (current prices, Nepal FY or Nepali month), INR converted with the NRB NPR_per_INR middle rate for the same month; industrial tariffs grossed back to the generator busbar with the busbar-to-meter loss factor, export price netted to the busbar per 22E.

Average VA per GWh from the manufacturing census is an upper bound for marginal VA; the lower bound is the price actually paid for electricity (cost-minimising firms value the marginal kWh at its price). Marginal VA for a new plant is computed project-by-project as (gross output - non-electricity intermediate inputs) per GWh, less annualised capital charge and labour at a shadow wage.

Demand charges are converted to per-kWh equivalents only through an explicit load-factor and power-factor range per industry (e.g. continuous-process vs single-shift vs flexible), reported as a sensitivity range.

Electric cooking and electric transport are evaluated as import substitution (avoided LPG/petroleum imports), not as industrial value added, and are labelled as such when entered in MarginalUseComparison.

Reliability requirement classes: (R1) continuous-process loads intolerant of interruptions (steel melting, cement kilns, data centres); (R2) shift-based loads tolerant of scheduled interruptions (cement grinding, re-rolling); (R3) flexible/interruptible loads that can follow wet-season surplus (electrolysers, managed EV charging, water pumping). Classes are a modelling assumption to be confirmed with the sources.

data_gaps: Every empirical value: no primary document downloaded in r1.
ERC tariff order vintage in force for FY2082/83-FY2083/84 unconfirmed (shared with 22E).
Whether NEA publishes SAIDI/SAIFI by distribution centre or feeder class is unconfirmed; may require a data request to NEA DCSD.
NIS 2019/20 report tables: whether electricity quantity (kWh) is published by ISIC industry or only expenditure; establishment-level microdata access terms unknown.
No Nepal-specific capital cost data for data centres, electrolytic hydrogen or ammonia; only international references (IEA/IRENA) with transfer assumptions.
Shadow wage for Nepal (needed for marginal VA net of labour) not located; depends on labour-market work by 10B/23 agents.
Block-level (hourly/15-minute) data needed to compare ToD tariffs with export/import prices in the same blocks.
Value of lost load for Nepali industry: no Nepal study located.
units.py lacks codes for NPR per kVA per month (demand charge), hours/minutes (SAIDI) and compound intensities (GWh per NPR mn).
WECS, MCA-Nepal, Uptime Institute and World Bank Enterprise Surveys are not (or not separately) in the source catalog.

assumptions.text: Tariff and export price compared at the generator busbar in NPR_per_MWh by month; INR via NRB middle NPR_per_INR rate for the same month.
Census average VA/GWh is an upper bound, electricity price paid a lower bound; project marginal VA is net of annualised capital and labour at shadow wage.
Demand charges converted to per-kWh only via explicit load-factor and power-factor ranges by requirement class.
Electric cooking and transport valued as import substitution, not industrial VA, and labelled so.
Reliability requirement classes R1 continuous / R2 shift / R3 flexible.
assumptions.basis_note: original label: 'assumption (to be confirmed with sources)'

challenges.text: Alignment: 05B will deliver T_IND (schedule, realised, implied paid), VA_IND (average, upper bound), K_IND by candidate and the reliability component of C_GRID; 05B does not reproduce the opportunity-cost table. Proposal: add a labour opportunity-cost deduction (labour cost x (1 - shadow-wage ratio) per GWh) to the domestic column; with emigration as the alternative for many workers, the shadow wage is not obviously low, and omitting it biases the domestic column upwards.

energy.MarginalUseComparison deducts annualised capital but not labour at shadow wage; propose an optional labour_opportunity_cost_per_gwh field. units.py: request codes for NPR per kVA per month (demand charges), hours/minutes (SAIDI/CAIDI) and a compound intensity code (GWh per NPR_current_mn). Source catalog: propose WECS (tier 1), World Bank Enterprise Surveys (tier 2), MCA-Nepal (tier 1/4), Uptime Institute (tier 7). NSO microdata exists on two hosts (microdata.nsonepal.gov.np and legacy microdata.cbs.gov.np); both should be accepted for the nso_nepal source.

Hand-off accepted: electricity-intensity classification by ISIC from NIS 2019/20 will be supplied for the RCA flag. Request: 05C RCA table should mark whether cement and steel RCA is driven by preferential access to India (tariff arbitrage), since this changes the marginal VA of new capacity.
05B needs the busbar-to-industrial-meter technical loss factor by voltage (LF_DOM) and dry-season available capacity, to gross up tariffs and to size firm supply for R1 loads.

Data-centre electricity use per MW and reliability/backup requirements: please share the IEA/Uptime references you retrieve; 05B treats data centres as R1 loads whose domestic value per GWh must net out foreign profit repatriation (GNI).
Electric cooking and transport are valued via avoided LPG/petroleum imports; 05B needs landed LPG and petroleum product prices (and any NOC subsidy) by month from the fuel-supply work.

Escalation: if the realised industrial tariff at the busbar is below the landed import cost in dry months, domestic industrial expansion implies a cross-subsidy funded by NEA; if wet-season spill is large, flexible (R3) loads may yield net national value even at low tariffs. Either finding would change electricity-led industrialisation proposals; r2 values must be audited before use.

Red-team note: continuous-process (R1) domestic industry is dependent on dry-season imports from India under time-limited approvals, so domestic use does not remove exposure to Indian approval decisions; it shifts it from export revenue to industrial continuity.

uncertainty: High: nothing retrieved. Structural uncertainties: (i) the gap between average and marginal VA per GWh is unknown and may be large, so the census ratio must never be used as the domestic value; (ii) the sign of tariff-minus-export-price plausibly changes by season and regime; (iii) demand-charge conversion depends on load factor, so all-in industrial tariffs are ranges; (iv) candidate industries without Nepal production (data centres, hydrogen/ammonia) rely on international transfer assumptions; (v) reliability baseline indices may not be published; (vi) the NIS 2019/20 reference year predates recent tariff and supply changes. No probabilities are assigned.

methodological_notes: The tariff is a transfer between the industry and NEA; for national value (energy.MarginalUseComparison) it enters only as part of the utility's output. The tariff-vs-export comparison answers NEA's revenue question, not the national value question.

Energy is metered at different points: industrial tariff at the consumer meter (after distribution losses), export price at the border metering point. Both are brought to the busbar before comparison.
Nepal FY (mid-July) tariff years vs Indian FY (April-March) price data: comparison is monthly, never annual-to-annual across fiscal bases.
Tariff-order vintages: a revision mid-year splits the Nepal FY; weight by months in force.

value_added_per_gwh.question: What is the value added per GWh in candidate domestic industries?
value_added_per_gwh.answer_status: pending - no census or project value retrieved in r1; method designed.
value_added_per_gwh.unit: NPR_per_GWh (current prices, Nepal FY); constant-price version only with the NSO manufacturing deflator for the same base year
value_added_per_gwh.primary_source: NSO National Industrial Survey 2019/20 (11th round of the Census of Manufacturing Establishments series) and CME 2011/12 (10th round); leads 05B-L12, L13, L14. Census round and reference period to be confirmed on retrieval.

method.step1_average: VA_avg(i) = census value added (i) / electricity purchased (i) in GWh [kWh x 1e-6], by ISIC industry i; own generation (diesel/captive) excluded from denominator and reported separately; suppressed cells flagged.
method.step2_cost_share_lower_bound: Under cost minimisation the marginal product of electricity equals its price, so the private marginal value of a kWh to an existing firm is the price paid (T_IND_PAID). Extra national value beyond the tariff arises only from rents, un- or under-employed labour (shadow wage below market wage), or forex savings from import substitution.
method.step3_project_marginal: For a new plant: VA_marg = (gross output - non-electricity intermediate inputs) / annual GWh - K_IND - labour cost x (1 - shadow-wage ratio)/GWh; inputs from DoInd/IBN project data or labelled international references (IEA/IRENA), prices from customs import parity.
method.step4_distribution: Where microdata access is granted, compute establishment-level VA/GWh percentiles within each industry; the marginal entrant is proxied by the median or lower quartile, not the mean.
method.step5_seasonality: Recompute K_IND per GWh at the capacity factor feasible under each supply regime (year-round firm supply vs wet-season-only surplus).
method.step6_gdp_vs_gni: For foreign-owned plants (data centres, hydrogen) report VA and the share accruing to non-residents (profit repatriation) separately.

baseline_metrics.metric: SAIDI by distribution centre / feeder class
baseline_metrics.unit: none yet (hours per customer per year; code requested)

baseline_metrics.metric: Firm-reported outages per month, losses as share of sales, generator ownership
Voltage and frequency excursions at industrial feeders

grid_investments.item: Dedicated 33 kV / 11 kV industrial feeders and trunk lines (ERC tariff/contribution rules)
132/33 kV substations and transformer capacity at industrial corridors (corridor names are candidate labels from general knowledge, to be replaced by NEA nomenclature)
Bulk 220/400 kV reinforcement to load centres (overlaps 05A transmission register)
Dry-season firm supply for R1 loads: storage hydro or import capacity/approvals (overlaps 05A, 22E P_IMP)
Distribution transformer upgrades for household e-cooking and EV charging (evening peak)
On-site backup (data centres, continuous-process plants) - private cost included in K_IND

reliability_requirements.costing_method: C_GRID_rel(i) = annualised capex of dedicated supply / annual GWh of industry i + expected unserved energy x industrial value of lost load (customer damage function from Enterprise Survey losses-to-sales and the Allcott et al. method), minus avoided private backup cost. Delivered to 22E as the reliability part of C_GRID.
reliability_requirements.trade_off: R3 flexible loads can absorb wet-season spill at near-zero opportunity cost and low reliability cost but run at low capacity factor, raising K_IND per GWh; R1 loads have high capacity factor but require dry-season firm supply whose marginal source is imports (approval-dependent). The net result is pending and may differ by candidate.
